messages:
Priya Rao: RFC draft posted for Structured Tool Invocation v2: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfc/tool-invoke-v2
Priya Rao: Main open decisions: validation strictness, canonical error envelope, migration path for clients. Customers asking for per-field errors and graceful partial results.
Marco Liu: runtime note: keep wire format backward-compatible. Prefer permissive server behavior by default; strict validation opt-in via header or route flag.
Dana O'Neill: ML/runtime constraint: if a tool call fails mid-generation, KV-cache state must be well-defined. AC: model only continues when handler explicitly returns {continue:true}. Otherwise generation halts and surfaces error.
Priya Rao: Draft acceptance criteria (suggested):
- AC1: Stable invocation envelope: invocation_id, tool, result?, error?, errors?
- AC2: Non-breaking defaults: unknown/new fields ignored by default with warning semantics
- AC3: Support partial success per-argument with per-path error entries
- AC4: Customers can opt into strict schema validation per-route or via X-Redwood-Validate header
- AC5: Publish migration guide + client library patch with examples
Eli Chen: From customers: fintech needs both machine codes and human-readable codes for per-arg failures, plus retry guidance.
Marco Liu: example wire shapes:
```
Success:
{ "invocation_id": "inv-987", "tool": "fx_rates", "result": { "rate": 0.032 } }
Partial:
{ "invocation_id":"inv-988", "tool":"composite", "result": {"a": {"value": 1}, "b": null}, "errors": [{"path":"b","code":"DEPENDENCY_TIMEOUT","message":"b timed out"}] }
Failure:
{ "invocation_id":"inv-989", "tool":"addr_lookup", "error": {"code":"INVALID_ARG","message":"postal_code malformed"} }
```
Ben Stewart: Legal/security: redact PII from tool payloads in logs; in Dedicated/Private we must document KMS/HSM usage and how audit trails surface tokenized references only.
Sasha (eng-infra): rollout suggestion: hosted default to permissive. Provide header X-Redwood-Validate: strict. Canary 10% orgs for 48h, watch validation error rate and tail latency.
Priya Rao: Proposed phased scope:
- Phase 1 (MVP): envelope + structured errors + permissive validation + migration checklist + sample client patch
- Phase 2: strict-mode server validation + schema registry + CLI migration helpers + per-route telemetry
- Phase 3: schema-evolution helpers, server-side auto-fixes, compatibility tooling
Marco Liu: Edge cases to call out in RFC: unknown enum values, extra properties in nested objects, mixed-version client/server interactions, partial tool timeouts vs full invocation timeouts, idempotency in retries.
Dana O'Neill: ML concerns: tool side-effects affecting future generations. Add AC: side_effects must be declared; handlers should be replayable or clearly marked side_effect:true.
Eli Chen: Add deliverable: customer-facing error docs with mapping table for common error codes + recommended retry behavior.
Priya Rao: Scope negotiation question: is permissive-by-default + strict opt-in acceptable? Ill update RFC with the AC checklist and migration steps.
Marco Liu: +1
Dana O'Neill: +1
deploy-bot: canary toggle enabled for 10% orgs (id: can-20260323-01)
Priya Rao: Next actions: I will update the RFC with these ACs, add the sample responses above, and draft the migration checklist. @Marco @Dana can you review the updated draft when I push it today?
